Biology 2023 Higher Level, deferred sitting: reviewed task ledger, carded for the first time.

Independent visual sweep (2026-11-19), every page rendered and read:
  * LC025ALP038EV (deferredexams/2023; Sections A and B and Answerbook), 40 pages: p1 cover, p2
    instructions, p3-p9 Section A Questions 1-7, p10-p12 Section B Questions 8-10, p13 Section C
    answerbook instructions, p14-p15 graph paper, p16-p39 ruled answer pages, p40 back cover with the
    copyright notice.
  * LC025ALP040EV (Section C), 12 pages: p1 cover, p2-p10 Questions 11-17, p11 "Do not hand this
    question paper up", p12 back cover with the copyright notice.
  * LC025ALP000EV (deferredmarkingschemes/2023), 24 pages: p1 cover, p2 the deferred-scheme note, p3
    introduction, p4-p5 marking examples, p6 the annotations table, p7 the Irish-medium bonus table,
    p8-p21 Questions 1-17, p22-p23 "BLANK PAGE", p24 back cover.

The sitting has the June 2023 Higher shape (any five of Section A, any two of B, any four of C). The
deferred scheme sets out every printed ask, so no card needs the "prints no answer" row. Section A is
marked on one ladder per question, as printed: Q1 best five of six, 3(6) + 2(1); Q2 2(5) + 1(3) + 7(1)
over its five cases of two features each; Q3-Q6 2(5) + 5(2); Q7 2(5) + 4(2) + 2(1). Every response on a
ladder is carded at the ladder's first rate and counted against it (CHECKSUMS). Section B parts (a) 6
and (b) 24, and Section C parts (9), (27), (24) and Q16/Q17's 30s, carry the scheme's own per-row marks.
Drawings and marks on printed diagrams are criterion rows priced as printed. Two choice asks whose
options the scheme answers differently are ROUTES (Q7(g) arthritis or osteoporosis; Q17(b)(iv) paralysis
or Parkinson's disease); Q14(a)(ii)'s two disorders share one printed cause and treatment, so it is one
card. Numbered asks (Q14(c)(i)1-3, Q15(c)(iv)1-3, Q16(c)(v)1-2, Q16(d)(iv)1-2, Q16(d)(v)1-3,
Q17(a)(iii)1-2, Q17(b)(ii)1-3, Q17(b)(iii)1-2) are priced separately and carded one each. Q11(b)(i)'s
underlined term is shown on a crop of the printed passage and its ask, the pedigree between them
masked; Q12(b)(vi) carries the scheme's own pyramid of numbers as its solution figure.
SELECTION_SCAN: Instructions: "blue or black pen", not a question.
Section A rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section B rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section C rubric: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Q1 best five of (a)-(f) on one ladder: every part is carded.
Q2 "each of the following cases": every case asked, one card each.
Q7(a) "any one region": open single answer; one card.
Q8(b)(ii) "both grass and clover": both required; one card.
Q10(b)(i) "resting PR or resting BR": the scheme marks either on the same rows; one card.
Q10(b)(ii) "either pulse rate (PR) or breathing rate (BR)": marked on the same rows; one card.
Q10(b)(iii) "PR or BR": one answer for both; one card.
Q11(c)(iv) "anabolic or a catabolic": the answer options.
Q13(b) lead-in "autotrophic or heterotrophic": description, not a choice.
Q14(a)(ii) "either fibroids or endometriosis": the scheme prints the same cause and treatment for both; one card.
Q14(b)(vi) "both urine and sperm": the structure described, not a choice.
Q14(c)(i) "each of the following": each event asked, one card per item.
Q15(b)(iv) "both of these stages": both compared; one card.
Q16 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q16(b)(vi) "any two sense organs": bounded menu; one card.
Q16(b)(vii) "the eye or the ear": open choice of disorder; one card.
Q16(c)(v)2 "any three types of T cell": bounded menu; one card.
Q16(d)(i) "monocotyledonous or dicotyledonous": the answer options.
Q16(d)(ii) "Copy either seed": either seed, labelled the same; one card.
Q16(d)(ii) "label the following parts": every label asked; one card.
Q16(d)(iv) "each of the following parts": each part asked, one card per item.
Q16(d)(v) lead-in: every item asked, one card each.
Q17 "any two of (a), (b), (c), (d)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q17(b)(iv) "one of the following ... paralysis or Parkinson's disease": separate cause and treatment per option: ROUTES.
Q17(d) lead-in "mechanical or chemical": description, not a choice.

q3-carbon: Diagram of part of the carbon cycle: Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere at the top; arrows from it down to Plant carbohydrate (Photosynthesis), from Plant carbohydrate to Animal carbohydrate (Nutrition), from both down to Dead organic matter (Death and decay), from Dead organic matter to Fossil fuels; arrow B rises from the plant and animal boxes back up to the atmosphere, and arrow A rises from Fossil fuels, past a factory, back up to the atmosphere.
q4-chloroplast: Electron microscope photograph of a plant cell organelle: an oval body with an outer double membrane and many dark stacks of internal membranes.
q5-mitosis: Diagram of an animal cell in mitosis: spindle fibres stretch between two poles, and four X-shaped chromosomes are lined up across the middle of the cell.
q6-stem: Light microscope photograph of a transverse section of a stem: a round section with a ring of dark patches near its edge; one patch is boxed and labelled Vascular bundle, the outer edge is labelled Dermal tissue, and a box with the letter A stands beside the section.
q7-spine: Diagram of the vertebral column in side view, divided into five regions by dotted lines, with a box containing the letter D beside it.
q8-tables: Two tables of frequency data, Herbivore present and Herbivore absent, each with a row for Grass and a row for Clover and five columns of ticks and crosses. Herbivore present: Grass tick, cross, tick, cross, tick; Clover cross, tick, cross, tick, cross. Herbivore absent: Grass five ticks; Clover cross, tick, cross, tick, tick.
q9-graph: Graph of enzyme activity against a factor: a single sharp peak, with a dashed line down from the top of the peak, labelled Optimum activity.
q10-table: Table of the student\u2019s results, PR and BR: Resting 62 and 16; Moderate exercise 118 and 25; Intense exercise 150 and 45.
q11-nucleotide: Diagram of a nucleotide: a small circle labelled X joined to a pentagon labelled Y, joined to a two-ring shape bracketed as Nitrogenous base, with dashed lines from the base labelled Z.
q11-pedigree: Pedigree chart: the parents, a square (male) and a half-shaded circle (female); their four children numbered 1 to 4: a plain circle, a half-shaded circle, a plain square and a fully shaded square. A key reads: plain circle, female with red-green colour vision; half-shaded circle, heterozygous female; plain square, male with red-green colour vision; shaded square, male with red-green colour blindness.
q11b-passage: The printed passage of Question 11(b), in which the word allele is underlined: red-green colour blindness is a recessive, sex-linked characteristic caused by an allele on the X chromosome; N is the allele for red-green colour vision and n the recessive allele; the pedigree chart shows parents and their four children; then (i) Explain the underlined term.
q12-graphs: Three graphs of population (thousands) against time (in years, 0 to 30): Wildebeest, rising and falling between about 10 and 30 with peaks; Lion, low with sharp peaks reaching about 3 to 4; Zebra, rising and falling between about 10 and 30.
q12b-vi-scheme: The marking scheme\u2019s pyramid of numbers: three stacked bars, Phytoplankton at the base, Shrimp above it and Chub at the top.
q13-yeast: Diagram of a yeast cell with a bud: A points to the outer boundary of the cell, B to a large round body containing a dark spot, and C to a clear oval space inside the cell.
q14-male: Diagram of the male reproductive system and part of the urinary system in side view: A points to a gland below the bladder, B to a coiled tube on the testis, C to the penis, and X to the testis.
q15-mitochondrion: Transmission electron microscope image of an oval organelle with a double membrane and many folded internal membranes.
q15-atp: Diagram of the structure of ATP: a two-ring structure bracketed and labelled 1, joined to a pentagon labelled 2, joined to a chain of three small circles bracketed and labelled 3.
q16-carpel: Diagram of the carpel of a flower: a pollen grain on the stigma at the top, X points to the long stalk below the stigma, a bracket Y spans the swollen base, and Z points to a body inside it containing the egg cell.
q16-ear: Diagram of the internal structure of the human ear: Bone and Eustachian tube are labelled; A points to the looped canals of the inner ear, B to the coiled structure beside them, and C to the thin membrane at the end of the ear canal.
q16-blood: Light microscope photograph of blood cells: many pale round cells, two of them pointed to by X, and a larger cell with a dark nucleus labelled Lymphocyte.
q16-seeds: Diagrams of two seeds in section: seed A with a large region labelled Endosperm above a small embryo; seed B with two large kidney-shaped halves and a small embryo between them.
q17-adh: Graph of ADH concentration against time: the line stays low, then rises steeply and levels off high.
q17-brain: Diagram of the internal structure of the human brain in section: C points to the large folded upper part, B to the rounded part at the lower back, and A to the stem at the base.
q17-heart: Sketch of the internal parts of the human heart: A points to the large arched vessel leaving the top, F to a large vessel on the left of the picture, B to the upper chamber on the right of the picture, C to a valve below it, E to a valve at the base of a vessel, and D to the wall between the lower chambers.
q17-digestive: Diagram of the human digestive system in outline: D points into the mouth, A to the tube running down the neck and chest, B to the large organ on the left of the picture, C to a small sac beneath it, E to the bag-shaped organ on the right of the picture, and F to the wide tube around the coiled intestine.
